title: The Black Hole
abstract: The Black Hole turns a malfunctioning photocopier into a portable opening through solid surfaces. This analysis examines how the film trains viewers to understand its rule, then transforms curiosity into theft and entrapment.
image_captions: The late-night office establishes the film’s fluorescent baseline
The worker tests the impossible aperture on the copier lid
The printed circle first appears as an object before it becomes a portal
Close-up experimentation turns curiosity into method
The sheet becomes a portable tool once the rule is understood
The office’s ordinary geometry keeps the impossible effect legible
